title: Fatness and Flatness
summary: Fat minors are the metric analog of graph minors that are tailored to the analysis of metric (edge-weighted) graphs and, more generally, metric spaces having a suitable notion of shortest paths. Despite a large interest in this notion, not much is known about the structure of metric graphs excluding a fixed fat minor. We prove that if a metric graph $G$ excludes a fixed graph $H$ as a $δ$-fat minor, for some $δ>0$, then $G$ enjoys the metric analog of flatness (aka uniform quasi-wideness) - a structural property from the field of Sparsity.
